Despite the brevity of the script, both characters—Lukas and Marie—are portrayed as complex, round characters rather than flat plot devices. Through subtext, body language (Marie keeping her coat buttoned, stirring sugarless tea; Lukas kneading his napkin and avoiding eye contact), and brief references to their shared past, the author gives both characters distinct emotional depth, flaws, and motivations. Lukas shows vulnerability and regret, having learned from his past mistakes of overworking and acting rashly, while Marie displays a realistic mix of lingering hurt, guardedness, and self-awareness. Neither character exists solely to serve the other's arc; instead, their interaction feels like a believable, emotionally charged moment between two fully realized people.
